messages:
sofia: heads up — replay harness on prod traces shows ~12-18% p95 regression vs our synthetic client run for the same model and load. curious if anyone else sees this or has quick hypotheses :thinking_face:
mike: what exactly differs between the harnesses? connection behavior usually bites us first. single long-lived connections vs many short ones? TLS session reuse?
sofia: good q. synthetic uses long-lived pooled conns (keepalive enabled, pool size 50). replay opens a new conn per session to mirror user flows. also replay replays bursts that contain many short sequences — sequence len distribution differs.
jordan: that can change kernel selection in the runtime. short sequences often use a different attention kernel we optimized for cache-friendly batches, long sequences hit the other path — leads to different per-token perf. did you capture which kernel was chosen?
sofia: I ran a quick profile. perf-bot posted a snippet (attached) but TL;DR: under replay we saw increased time in "attn_qkv_transform" and more frequent small-batch kernels. stable bench used the fused large-batch kernel.
perf-bot: profiling summary: p95 latency +15%, cpu cycles in attn_qkv_transform +26%, KV cache hit ratio down from 82% -> 65% in replay scenario (likely due to session churn).
mike: KV cache drop makes sense if users are opening fresh sessions and model prefix reuse is low. More cache misses => more compute per request. Also connection churn increases TLS handshakes which add CPU and latency.
natalie: also check client TCP settings. Nagle + delayed ACKs can create micro-packets for short requests. For short prompt payloads we saw 10–20ms extra per-request when TCP_NODELAY was off.
sofia: yep. I toggled TCP_NODELAY in the replay harness and p95 improved ~6%. Removing TLS session reuse (to simulate worst-case) regressed another ~9%.
jordan: Parallelization/ batching heuristics also sensitive: synthetic harness batches many short requests into one host-side batch, replay had fewer coalesced requests because of timing jitter. Was our batching window the same in both runs?
sofia: batching window config was identical, but timing of arrivals differs so effective batch sizes were smaller in replay. I added a small jitter in synthetic and saw batch sizes drop and latency move closer to replay.
mike: to get apples-to-apples we need: 1) identical connection patterns (keepalive vs new), 2) identical arrival jitter, 3) same sequence length distribution, 4) same auth/TLS reuse behavior. Only then can we attribute perf diff to kernel selection or runtime regression.
natalie: quick reproducer idea: run two harness modes — "sticky-conns" (long-lived) and "stateless" (new conn per session) with same trace arrival timings and prefix distributions. capture: kernel selection logs, KV cache hits, TLS handshake counts, and per-token CPU.
sofia: done a first pass — uploading logs to the perf bucket. Link: s3://redwood-perf/replays/1838274000/ (I pasted the important excerpts below).
mike: can you paste the client config you used for the replay? helps sanity check keepalive/tls settings.
sofia: config snippet:
```
client: {
  connections: "per-session",
  tcp_keepalive: false,
  tcp_nodelay: true,
  tls_session_resumption: disabled,
  concurrency: 60,
  arrival_jitter_ms: 20
}
```
jordan: good. Also try gRPC vs HTTP/1.1 toggles. gRPC (HTTP/2) keeps multiplexed streams on single conn which improves reuse but has head-of-line blocking tradeoffs; HTTP/1.1 with many conns creates TLS churn. We should run both and compare kernel selection & KV hit ratios.
natalie: FYI: we once blamed a runtime regression that was actually caused by the test harness opening ephemeral conns; fixed the harness and the regression disappeared :facepalm:. Lesson: harness parity matters.
sofia: action items I propose: 1) add a harness mode that replays real connection churn from live traces, 2) instrument client to emit TLS handshake counts and tcp_nodelay state, 3) add microbench isolating TLS vs model compute (run with dummy kernel to measure net overhead), 4) run apples-to-apples long-lived vs churned with identical arrival & prompt distribution.
mike: +1. Also add a small test toggling TCP_NODELAY and measuring small-payload RTTs; document the impact in the benchmark guide.
jordan: and capture kernel selection mapping in the runtime logs so we can correlate which kernel executed with batch sizes/sequence lengths. That will tell us if the runtime is choosing a suboptimal kernel under the new arrival patterns.
sofia: I'll kick off the systematic runs this afternoon and post numbers. thanks for the quick feedback. :thumbsup:
mike: thanks — ping here when the runs finish, and if possible tag the perf-alert channel if p95 > baseline +10% so we can triage quickly.
perf-bot: scheduled job started: perf-replay-1838274000 — collecting: kernel-map, kv-stats, tls-handshakes, batch-stats — ETA ~40m.
